Seminar Title:

A Two-Tier Secured Underwater Wireless Optical Communication Link: Joint Physical Layer Security and Covert Communication

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Neetu Khunte ( Rollno : 524ec1005)

10 Nov 2026 05:30 PM

Contact:

Prasad Naik Ramavath

Abstract:

Transmitting sensitive/confidential information requires high security as well as reliability. Transmitting such confidential information across free-space using the radio-frequency (RF) signals increases the risk of interception and eavesdropping. Rather than relying on the free-space channels, leveraging less explored underwater channels can help to enhance the integrity of the information by ensuring the reliability using the sophisticated communication technologies. In underwater environment, RF signals are highly attenuated and acoustic signals are restricted to lower data-rates. Hence, we are proposing optical signals to transmit in underwater, which offers high data-rates and low latency compared to acoustic and less attenuation compared to RF. However, underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) is limited to short-to-medium link-ranges due to the challenges, such as underwater turbulence, beam attenuation effects, pointing errors and signal blockage. In addition these challenges, we have considered an eavesdropper, who tries to decode the message and a warden (Willie) who tries to detect the presence of transmission. In order to maintain the information integrity from the Eve, a physical layer security (PLS) assisted UWOC proposed, which requires high transmit power. Similarly, to prevent from the Willie, covert communication approach used, which requires low power to transmit the information thus, these two goals conflict and must be designed simultaneously. In this work, we considered an UWOC link that simultaneously achieves both goals. The link uses intensity modulation with direct detection (IM/DD) over an exponential generalized Gamma (EGG) turbulence channel with pointing errors and blockage.
